final_candidates.decision_summary: Verified WT Ile at position 34 in the HA1 head; conservative Ile-to-Leu maintains hydrophobic burial and may improve local packing with minimal structural disruption.
Verified WT Thr at position 30; replacing a polar threonine with hydrophobic isoleucine increases buried hydrophobic surface, a commonly stabilizing direction if the site is core-facing.
Verified WT Val at position 43; conservative Val-to-Leu slightly increases hydrophobic volume in the N-terminal region, likely aiding core packing without altering charge or backbone geometry.

stop_reason.detail: LLM-only control with no evidence tools; candidate pool already reflects converged first-principles stability ranking.

history.rationale: Leu-for-Ile substitution in an early hydrophobic region may improve van der Waals packing in the HA1 core with minimal structural disruption. Conservative hydrophobe swap preserves viability.
Conservative Ile-to-Leu in HA1 head; verified WT I34 in sequence. Likely stabilizes local hydrophobic packing with minimal structural risk.
Adding a larger hydrophobic side chain at Val43 could strengthen local hydrophobic packing. Ile/Leu enlargement of buried Val positions is a common mild thermostabilizing strategy.
Verified WT V43; conservative hydrophobic substitution near the N-terminal region may improve core packing without disrupting function.
Gly-to-Ala reduces backbone conformational entropy and often stabilizes if the site is not in a tight loop. Moderate risk if position is surface-exposed or in a turn.
Verified WT G49; Gly-to-Ala reduces backbone flexibility, which typically confers modest thermostabilization if not at a required hinge.
Very conservative Ile-to-Val near a predicted cysteine-containing region; unlikely to destabilize and could relieve local steric strain. Low expected gain but low risk.
Verified WT I51; conservative swap but slightly reduces side-chain volume, giving weaker expected stabilization.
Ala-to-Val enlargement in the N-terminal hydrophobic segment may improve core packing. Risk of overpacking or interfering with N-terminal processing keeps confidence moderate.
Verified WT A11 near N-terminus; Ala-to-Val increases hydrophobicity, but the region is near the signal-cleavage/N-terminal zone so benefit is uncertain.
Thr-to-Ile increases hydrophobicity in a conserved N-terminal motif; if partially buried this could add stability. Could be deleterious if the Thr makes H-bonds.
Position 30 verified as Thr; Thr-to-Ile adds hydrophobic burial in the head domain and is a common stabilizing direction, so confidence raised.
Asp-to-Asn removes a surface negative charge that may reduce electrostatic repulsion or desolvation penalty. Effect likely small; speculative without structural data.
Verified WT D7; Asp-to-Asn removes a surface charge which could reduce solubility stability, so kept at low confidence.
Ser-to-Thr is a conservative change that can slightly increase local hydrophobic contact. Weak expected effect; included mainly as a low-risk baseline candidate.
Verified WT S9; Ser-to-Thr is conservative but near-neutral for folding stability, hence lowest rank.
